title: Solve using the quadratic formula with exact roots

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: Identify coefficients from ax^2 + bx + c: here a = 2, b = 3, c = -2.
Because c = -2, the term -4ac becomes -4(2)(-2), which is positive.

hint_ladder.title: What must be identified first?
hint_ladder.prompt: The quadratic formula depends on a, b, and c from standard form. Before calculating, identify each coefficient carefully.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Write the formula structure and substitute the three coefficients, paying special attention to any negative signs.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: When c is negative, check the sign of the -4ac part before simplifying the discriminant.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0, use x = (-b ? sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / 2a. Substitute symbols first, then simplify. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

common_errors: drops the negative sign on c
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is identifying a, b, and c correctly.
The stuck point is substituting signs and denominator into the formula.
The stuck point is simplifying both formula results.

mark_scheme_notes: Award marks for coefficients, formula substitution, discriminant, and both roots.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: sign error in -4ac and denominator 2a.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what are a, b, and c?
